title: Uniform local-model Tor bounds extend across finite constructible strata
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$: a finite discrete commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or one of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is a finite subextension of $\Qlb$, with the condensed objects of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Fix integers $c\leq d$. Suppose that for every scheme $S$, every $\Lambda_S$-module having a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Then for every qcqs scheme $X$, every constructible $\Lambda_X$-module [sk-def-sfb-constructible] has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. The constructible stratification is a finite partition by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], with no assumption that its strata are globally open or reduced.

source.place: Strata, local induction on the number of strata replacing the unsupported globally open-stratum choice

proof.text: Choose a finite constructible stratification $s_a:S_a\hookrightarrow X$ for $M$, so that $M_a=s_a^*M$ has a finite constant local model. Apply [lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement] to this one partition. It gives a finite rooted binary tree, with root $X$, qcqs vertices $T$, and structure maps $t_T:T\to X$. Each internal vertex is split into a quasi-compact open child and its closed complement. For each nonempty leaf $T$, choose the actual factorization $t_T=s_a\circ h_T$ through a stratum supplied by the lemma. This uses the scheme-theoretic factorization in its statement, not a factorization inferred merely from containment of images.

source.place: Tag 09Y4, lemma-constructible-partition-refined-by-stratification; use its existing scheme-theoretic binary refinement node

proof.text: Fix a nonempty leaf and its map $h_T:T\to S_a$. Choose a model cover $V_\lambda\to S_a$ and scalar matrices $A_\lambda$ presenting $M_a|_{V_\lambda}$ as $\operatorname{coker}(\Lambda_{V_\lambda}^{m_\lambda}\xrightarrow{A_\lambda}\Lambda_{V_\lambda}^{n_\lambda})$ by [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Base change gives a pro-etale cover $W_\lambda=T\times_{S_a}V_\lambda\to T$, by the covering-preserving base-change assertion of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], pullback is exact and identifies the pulled-back coefficient ring with $\Lambda_{W_\lambda}$; hence it sends this cokernel to $\operatorname{coker}(\Lambda_{W_\lambda}^{m_\lambda}\xrightarrow{A_\lambda}\Lambda_{W_\lambda}^{n_\lambda})$. The entries remain the same elements of $\Lambda(*)$, since their actions are pulled back along the structure maps from the point. The composition comparison [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] identifies these modules with $(t_T^*M)|_{W_\lambda}$. The matrix criterion therefore proves that $t_T^*M$ has a finite constant local model. This is the direct application of an exact functor to a finite presentation.

source.place: Matrix-presentation criterion, clause 2; pull back the presentation on the base-changed cover

proof.text: Apply the hypothesis of the item with $S=T$ to every nonempty leaf, using step 2: $t_T^*M$ has Tor amplitude in the original interval $[c,d]$. For an empty leaf (or an empty root), the empty family is a pro-etale cover: all weakly etale conditions are vacuous, and every affine open is empty and is covered by the empty finite family, as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. The definition [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] therefore gives a finite constant local model for its restricted module, with no matrices to choose. Apply the same hypothesis on this empty scheme. Thus the assertion holds at every leaf, including the empty cases, without any assumption that $0\in[c,d]$.

source.place: Strata; leaf case of the finite induction, including empty strata

proof.text: Induct upwards on the finite tree (equivalently, on the height of the subtree below a vertex). The induction assertion at a vertex $T$ is that $M_T=t_T^*M$, in degree zero, has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. Step 3 proves the height-zero case. At an internal vertex let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be its open and closed child maps. The induction hypotheses give the assertion for the two child restrictions of $M$. By [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] these are $j^*M_T$ and $i^*M_T$. The canonical coefficient isomorphisms and exact inverse-image description in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify these with the restrictions over $j^{-1}\Lambda_T$ and $i^{-1}\Lambda_T$ required by [lem-sfb-tor-interval-local-detection](ii). Its open immersion is quasi-compact by step 1, so that lemma applies to $K=M_T[0]$ over the sheaf of rings $\Lambda_T$, and proves the same Tor interval at $T$. Tor amplitude is invariant under the displayed isomorphisms by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. This proves the induction assertion. At the root the restricted module is $M$, which is the desired conclusion. Each use keeps $[c,d]$ unchanged; no bound grows with the number of vertices.

source.place: Strata; finite open-closed induction, using the refinement rather than assuming an original stratum is open

Wrote out the elementary pullback of scalar-matrix local models and a finite-tree induction, including empty and nonreduced cases. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Strata paragraph of det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc: local models on strata, exact open-closed detection, and finite induction. Repairs the unsupported globally open-stratum choice using the existing refinement theorem.

tool_uses.why: Generic geometric refinement of a finite constructible locally closed partition into actual complementary open/closed pullbacks. The unit has no such refinement statement; its local-model and localization route is retained.

Only the untwisted coefficient isomorphism and exact inverse-image description for arbitrary scheme morphisms are used to pull back matrices and identify restriction rings. This is coefficient transport needed by the unit, not a replacement of its route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-974397020 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's 4 steps in full against every cited statement; no repairs. Shape: one commit; statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint unchanged from the side base; no new nodes; proof_deps = union of uses; no cycle in a 3147-node closure; no SGA; item not in any drop list; no repair note, so not a re-split. Source error confirmed: the blueprint's Strata paragraph chooses an open stratum, but a finite constructible locally closed partition need not have one. Counterexample checked: on A1 ⊔ A1', the strata (A1∖0)⊔{0'} and {0}⊔(A1'∖0') are each locally closed and constructible, and neither is open. Step 1: lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement (reviewed PASS by Q89) states, for qcqs X and one partition, a binary tree with quasi-compact open children and an actual morphism from each nonempty leaf to a stratum; I checked Stacks 09Y4. Step 2 (elementary): the matrix criterion of det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model, the covering-preserving base change of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, the exact pullback and alpha iso of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients (alpha comes from f^*p_Y^*≅p_X^*, so scalar entries stay scalar) and def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp give the leaf a finite constant local model. Step 3: the item hypothesis on nonempty leaves; on empty leaves the empty family is a pro-étale cover per def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering, so no assumption 0∈[c,d] is needed. Step 4: the induction is fully set up and uses lem-sfb-tor-interval-local-detection (ii), which needs a quasi-compact open (true, Stacks 09AH allows any closed subscheme, so nonreduced children are fine); [c,d] is never enlarged. Both declared tool uses (the refinement node and the cartesian-coefficients node) are accepted as generic geometry and coefficient transport. Edge cases tested: one stratum, X empty, nonreduced and disconnected strata, Z/ℓ² (the hypothesis fails for F_ℓ, so no false consequence), Q̄_ℓ. No duplicate of the item found in the DAG.
